summary: Backend-only testing of the Weight & Metabolism GUIDED coaching upgrade (schedule pivot + day-plan timeline + auto water logging). Created 22 pytest cases covering schedule PUT (new+legacy forms), validations, day-plan computation, event check-in toggling, water auto-logging and _id leak prevention. All 22/22 tests PASSED.
critical_code_review_comments: Minor: `update_schedule` uses `if req.fast_start and req.fast_duration_hours` — since `fast_duration_hours=0` is invalid anyway this is fine, but a partial payload (fast_start only, no duration) falls through to legacy branch and then 400s; consider a clearer error message.
Minor: In `check_day_plan_event`, water auto-log uses a broad `except Exception: pass`. This silently hides DB errors; at least log them.

Minor: `water_intake_logs` entries have no uniqueness constraint; rapidly tapping the same event would insert no duplicate since check-in upsert is idempotent BUT water inserts fire each time a user tickles done->undone->done, double-logging water. Consider conditional insert or a `source` + `date` upsert.

Design: Event 'status' uses server UTC clock (same caveat already documented in get_schedule). For DE users (Europe/Berlin) event times displayed may be off by 1–2h depending on TZ. Client-side TZ handling is required.
Minor: File weight_metabolism.py is 1259 lines — consider splitting (goals, meals, fasting, schedule/day-plan, photo AI) into submodules per the 700-line guideline.
seed_data_creation: Profiles prefixed TEST_pid_* created in fasting_schedule, day_plan_checkins, water_intake_logs collections.
context_for_next_testing_agent: GUIDED Weight&Metabolism backend verified end-to-end. Schedule accepts both new (fast_start+fast_duration_hours 10-22) and legacy (eating_window_start+eating_window_hours 1-14) forms. Day-plan returns 4 events [shake1=start, small_meal=+45m, shake2=+mid, large_meal=end-90m] with water_ml [300,300,300,400]. POST /day-plan/check toggles check-in, auto-inserts water_intake_logs with source='day_plan_<key>'. No _id leaks. Remaining concern: double water-insert if user toggles done->undone->done (see code review).
